nodes.summary: On a ring of $n + 1$ processes with identifiers $\mathrm{id}$, process $k$ receives the oldest message in its channel in state $s$. If the channel of $k$ is empty there is no step. Otherwise let $j$ be the origin of that message, which is removed from the channel: if $\mathrm{id}(k) < \mathrm{id}(j)$, process $k$ forwards it by appending $j$ to the end of the channel of its successor on the ring; otherwise, if…
nodes.title: Delivering a message in the Chang–Roberts ring

nodes.summary: For processes $j$ and $m$ on a ring of $n + 1$ processes numbered $0, \dots, n$, the gap from $j$ to $m$ is the number of successor steps from $j$ to $m$: it is $m - j$ if $j \le m$, and $m + (n + 1) - j$ otherwise. It lies in $[0, n]$.
nodes.title: Forward distance on the ring

nodes.summary: In the initial state the channel into each process $k$ holds exactly one message, whose origin is the predecessor of $k$ on the ring (so every process has sent its identifier to its successor), and no process is leader.
nodes.title: Initial state of the Chang–Roberts ring

nodes.summary: For every assignment of identifiers, if the invariant holds in a state $s$ and the state $t$ is reached from $s$ by delivering messages along some schedule of receiving processes (a multistep transition of the algorithm's labelled transition system), then the invariant holds in $t$.
nodes.title: The Chang–Roberts invariant is preserved along runs

nodes.summary: For every assignment of identifiers, every state reachable from the initial state satisfies the invariant.
nodes.title: The Chang–Roberts invariant holds in every reachable state

nodes.summary: Given identifiers $\mathrm{id}$ on a ring of $n + 1$ processes, a state satisfies the invariant when two conditions hold. First, for every message from origin $j$ waiting in the channel of process $k$, every process $m \ne j$ that the message has already passed has a smaller identifier, $\mathrm{id}(m) < \mathrm{id}(j)$; here $m$ has been passed when its forward distance from $j$ is less than the distance the…
nodes.title: The Chang–Roberts invariant

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{id}$ assign a natural-number identifier, not necessarily distinct, to each process $0, \dots, n$ of the Chang–Roberts ring. In every state reachable with these identifiers, if process $i$ has declared itself leader, then $\mathrm{id}(m) < \mathrm{id}(i)$ for every process $m \ne i$.
nodes.title: Only the maximum is elected

nodes.summary: In every state of the Chang–Roberts algorithm reachable from the initial state, any two processes that have declared themselves leader are equal.
nodes.title: There is at most one leader

nodes.summary: For identifiers $\mathrm{id}$, the algorithm is the labelled transition system whose states are the global states and whose labels are processes: there is a transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled $k$ exactly when delivering the oldest message in the channel of process $k$ in state $s$ gives $t$.
nodes.title: The Chang–Roberts transition system

nodes.summary: On a ring of $n + 1$ processes numbered $0, \dots, n$, the predecessor of $k$ is $k - 1$ if $k \ne 0$, and $n$ if $k = 0$.
nodes.title: Predecessor on the ring

nodes.summary: Given a natural-number identifier $\mathrm{id}(k)$ for each process $k$ of the ring of $n + 1$ processes, a global state $s$ is reachable when the Chang–Roberts transition system with these identifiers leads from the initial state to $s$ by a multistep transition along some finite list of labels, that is, of receiving processes.
nodes.title: Reachable states of Chang–Roberts

nodes.summary: Given a natural-number identifier $\mathrm{id}(k)$ for each process $k$ of the ring, for all global states $s, t$ and every list $\kappa$ of processes, running the schedule $\kappa$ from $s$ returns $t$ if and only if the Chang–Roberts transition system with identifiers $\mathrm{id}$ has a multistep transition from $s$ to $t$ labelled by $\kappa$.
nodes.title: Runs are multistep transitions

nodes.summary: Given a natural-number identifier $\mathrm{id}(k)$ for each process $k$ of the ring, a global state $s$ and a list $k_1, \dots, k_r$ of processes, the run applies the Chang–Roberts delivery step at $k_1$, then at $k_2$, and so on. It returns the final state, or no state as soon as some $k_i$ has an empty channel at its turn; on the empty list it returns $s$.
nodes.title: Running a delivery schedule

nodes.summary: For a ring of $n + 1$ processes $0, \dots, n$, a global state assigns to each process $k$ the FIFO channel of messages waiting at $k$, oldest first, where each message is the index of the process whose identifier it carries, and records for each process whether it has declared itself leader.
nodes.title: Chang–Roberts global states

nodes.summary: On the ring of $n + 1$ processes $0, \dots, n$, the successor of process $k$ is $k + 1$ when $k < n$, and $0$ when $k = n$.
nodes.title: Successor on the Chang–Roberts ring

nodes.summary: For every process $k$ of the ring, the distance travelled by a message from the predecessor of $k$ waiting at $k$ is $1$.
nodes.title: The initial messages have travelled one link

nodes.summary: For processes $j$ and $k$ of the ring with $k \ne j$, the distance travelled by a message from $j$ waiting at the successor of $k$ is the number of links from $j$ forward to $k$, plus one.
nodes.title: Forwarding adds one link

nodes.summary: For processes $j, k$ of the ring of $n + 1$ processes, the distance travelled by a message from $j$ waiting at $k$ is $n + 1$, the whole ring, when $k = j$, and otherwise the ring distance from $j$ to $k$, the number of links from $j$ forward to $k$.
nodes.title: Distance travelled by a message

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
